title: Cook membrane: finite-strain F-bar convergence, standard-brick setup, and small-load limit
source: OpenGeoSys, Cook's membrane F-bar benchmark (Wang and Nagel, page revised 2024-07-03), https://www.opengeosys.org/stable/docs/benchmarks/large-deformations/cooksmembranefbar/; the five published displacement values and the comparison tolerance are transcribed from that page's code and the material input from its text; the geometry and the 100 N/mm edge shear are the classical Cook membrane (R. D. Cook, 1974), and the standard-brick rows confirm that this set-up is the benchmark's.

quantities.quantity: F-bar top-corner vertical displacement, 4 elements per side
quantities.reason: The public benchmark itself allows 2e-4 m for the F-bar comparison; this covers the coarse-mesh difference between independent F-bar implementations while the three meshes show convergence.

quantities.quantity: F-bar top-corner vertical displacement, 10 elements per side
quantities.reason: The public benchmark itself allows 2e-4 m for the F-bar comparison; this covers the coarse-mesh difference between independent F-bar implementations while the three meshes show convergence.

quantities.quantity: F-bar top-corner vertical displacement, 30 elements per side
quantities.reason: The public benchmark itself allows 2e-4 m for the F-bar comparison; this covers the coarse-mesh difference between independent F-bar implementations while the three meshes show convergence.

quantities.quantity: standard-brick top-corner vertical displacement, 4 elements per side
quantities.reason: The same public mesh and loading with F-bar disabled differ from the published standard-brick values by about 1e-4 relative; 5e-4 leaves a bounded comparison margin without masking a setup error.

quantities.quantity: standard-brick top-corner vertical displacement, 10 elements per side
quantities.reason: The same public mesh and loading with F-bar disabled differ from the published standard-brick values by about 1e-4 relative; 5e-4 leaves a bounded comparison margin without masking a setup error.

quantities.quantity: F-bar small-load response times 1000 over linear B-bar response
quantities.reason: At one-thousandth load the F-bar response is compared with the same 10-per-side mesh solved by linear B-bar; the 5e-4 bound is the requested nonuniform-state small-strain consistency check and is not an independent public reference.
